summary: Confirmed DONE. #710 (60633eff3, also in the Hub's vendored 7bc39eec3) removed the alphabetical dirs-then-files slice(0, 25_000). The search corpus is now every listed path, capped at 200k per VCS root; past that cap, shallower paths are kept. The 25k cap now applies only to the listEntries payload (shallowest entries). The ls-files byte cap went from 16 to 32 MiB, and truncation flows into index.partial. search() returns partial, the web client stops narrowing partial results from its cache, and the @ menu shows 'Showing results from part of the workspace.' both under results and under an empty result. A regression test with 30k files finds the last file. I found no correctness hole in the composer picker path. What is left are small follow-ups and policy nits, listed under fixDefects.

evidence.note: WORKSPACE_INDEX_MAX_ENTRIES = 200_000 is the search corpus cap, separate from WORKSPACE_LIST_ENTRIES_MAX = 25_000 (line 80). The global budget is 300k entries across 32 roots (lines 70-71); the old code allowed 4 roots of 25k each.
indexListedFiles does not sort. It builds every file plus its ancestor directories and calls selectShallowestFiles only when the total exceeds 200k (lines 504-511), setting partial in that case.
selectShallowestFiles: buckets by depth, keeps listing order within a depth (tracked before untracked), and stops at the budget. Depth takes priority over tracked status.
buildWorkspaceListing caps only the listEntries payload, using selectShallowestEntries. The kept set is a consistent tree, because parents are always shallower than their children.
search() ranks all index.entries and returns truncated = partial || matchedCount > limit, plus partial: true when the index is partial.
The listing's truncated flag (or tracked-only mode) is passed in as index partial.
WORKSPACE_FILES_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES = 32 MiB, applied to each of the three concurrent ls-files runs. listWorkspaceFiles (line 557) emits tracked paths before untracked ones and ORs the truncated flags.
narrowFromCache refuses to narrow a cached prefix result that is truncated or partial, so local narrowing cannot hide files.
pathResults.partial is passed to resolveComposerPathMenuEmptyState (composerPathMenu.ts:73). ComposerCommandMenu.tsx:236-249 renders the footnote under an empty result and under the result list.

Regression test: 30k files, the last file is found, partial is undefined, and the listEntries payload is capped at 25k with shallow-first ordering. Lines 399-460 cover partial for the tracked-files fallback and stand-in. No test covers the 200k selectShallowestFiles path or listing.truncated -> partial.
The non-VCS filesystem fallback still stops at 25k entries in BFS order. It is now shallow-first like the VCS path and flagged partial, but its search corpus is still limited to 25k.

Adjacent surface, not the composer: the File Preview 'Filter files' box filters the 25k-capped listEntries payload on the client, so deep files in large repos cannot be found there. It shows a 'Workspace tree is truncated' alert but does not fall back to searchEntries.

Adjacent surface: the mobile file search footer says 'Showing the first matches only. Narrow the search to see more.' whenever truncated is set. That is misleading when the index itself is partial, and mobile ignores the partial flag.

fixDefects: No correctness defect in the composer picker fix. Minor points: (1) Policy nit: past 200k entries, selectShallowestFiles (WorkspaceEntries.ts:177-199) lets depth beat tracked status. A repo with a huge untracked, non-ignored, shallow directory (data dumps, un-ignored venv or vendored SDK) can fill the cap with untracked files and drop deep tracked sources. The proposal asked for tracked before untracked. (2) Perf cost of the fix: search() ranks the whole corpus in one synchronous loop with no yield (WorkspaceEntries.ts:1268). On 200k synthetic paths (average 57 chars) rankWorkspaceEntries took about 18-42 ms per query on this machine, roughly 8x the old 25k cost. Short queries come back truncated, so the client cannot narrow them and every keystroke reaches the server. The build path is also only partly chunked: selectShallowestFiles plus entry construction took about 60 ms unyielded for a 450k listing (lines 504-519). The heap cost is about 33 MB per 200k-entry root, bounded by the 300k global budget. (3) The non-VCS fallback corpus is still 25k (line 78), flagged partial. (4) No test covers the 200k cap or the listing.truncated -> partial path. (5) Adjacent, outside the composer: the PreviewPanel filter is limited to the listEntries payload, and the mobile files search footer ignores partial.
implementationSketch: Optional follow-ups, all small. (a) In WorkspaceEntries.ts selectShallowestFiles, take a trackedCount (pass it from GitVcsDriver.listWorkspaceFiles as an extra result field, e.g. trackedPathCount, or split paths into tracked and untracked arrays in VcsListWorkspaceFilesResult). Fill the budget with tracked files by depth first, then untracked files by depth. Test it in WorkspaceEntries.index.test.ts with a fake listing of shallow untracked files above 200k plus deep tracked files, and assert the deep tracked file is searchable and partial is true. (b) Make search yield on large corpora: in WorkspaceEntries.search, rank in chunks of about 20k with Effect.yieldNow between chunks (add a resumable rankWorkspaceEntries accumulator in packages/shared/src/workspaceEntrySearch.ts, or rank per chunk and merge the top-N lists). Also chunk the entry construction loop in indexListedFiles. Add a unit test that ranking in chunks gives the same result as a single pass. (c) Add a test for listing.truncated=true -> search().partial === true. (d) Adjacent: in PreviewPanel, when listEntries is truncated and the filter query is non-empty, route the filter through projects.searchEntries (the same atom the composer uses). In mobile threadFilesModel/ThreadFilesScreen, show a 'part of the workspace' note when results.partial is set, instead of 'narrow the search'.
decisionReason: The finding is resolved. The tracked-first vs depth-first cap ordering is a small policy choice that only matters past 200k entries. It does not touch auth, E2EE, hosted lifecycle, or the Hub protocol.
